items.claim: Controlled path ignores nativeEvent.defaultPrevented, so a prevented change now clears errors and validates once the consumer echoes the value
items.consequence: onChange returns early for controlled values before the defaultPrevented check. When the consumer echoes the value via onValueChange, useValueChanged runs clearErrors, setDirty, setFilled and validation.change unconditionally, so the same prevented event has different field-state consequences for controlled and uncontrolled controls. Base behavior skipped validation for prevented controlled changes.
items.proposed_fix: Record the prevented/canceled state in onChange (e.g. a ref) and have the useValueChanged callback skip clearErrors/validation.change for that change, or keep the defaultPrevented gate for controlled values; add a controlled variant of the 'does not clear errors or validate when change is prevented' test.

evidence: Field.Root validationMode=onChange with validate, Field.Control value={v} onValueChange={setV}.
A capture listener preventDefaults the change event, as in the existing uncontrolled test.
onChange calls onValueChange (setV runs) then returns at the isControlled branch without reading defaultPrevented.
The value prop changes, useValueChanged fires and clears errors and validates; the uncontrolled variant asserts validate is not called.

items.claim: Uncontrolled details.cancel() still sets dirty/filled while skipping clearErrors and validation
items.consequence: The PR states cancel() now stops internal handling, but setDirty and setFilled run before the isCanceled gate. After a canceled uncontrolled keystroke the input shows the text, the field reads dirty and filled, and errors and validity are not refreshed. The only new cancel test asserts validate was not called.
items.proposed_fix: Decide and document what cancel means for the uncontrolled path (the DOM value cannot be reverted): either gate setDirty/setFilled on !details.isCanceled too, or state that cancel only suppresses validation and error clearing. Add a test asserting data-dirty/data-filled after a canceled uncontrolled change.

Result: data-dirty and data-filled set, DOM keeps 'a', stale errors remain.

native_payload.intent: Make Field.Control sync controlled value changes with field state through useValueChanged, like its sibling controls. This fixes the dirty baseline for non-string values by registering the serialized value. onChange owns the uncontrolled path and returns early when controlled, and details.cancel() now stops internal handling.

residual_risks: Non-string controlled values now reach Field validate() at submit/imperative validation and validityData.initialValue as String(value) (FieldControl.tsx:86 `const serializedValue = value == null ? undefined : String(value);`); a validator checking typeof v === 'number' changes behavior. Form onSubmit values are unaffected because getValue still reads the DOM. Likely intended (change-time validation already received strings) but a silent contract shift.

The dirty baseline is captured once on first registration, so a controlled value populated later by a fetch or a form-library reset(serverValues) marks the field dirty and, in onChange mode, validates before user interaction (FieldControl.tsx:111). Matches sibling controls; not verified against them here.

Controlled value={null} is still 'controlled' but serializes to undefined, so useValueChanged returns early and filled/dirty/validity stay stale on a transition to null (FieldControl.tsx:106). Edge case; React itself treats null as uncontrolled.

Async validators and validationDebounceTime now also apply to programmatic controlled changes; only the typing path is tested. Effect ordering was checked: no stale-closure issue found in validation.change called from the layout effect.

Controlled reset to '' keeps markedDirtyRef true (never cleared), so a required field in onChange mode can show 'Required' right after reset; the same happens today when a user types and clears in the uncontrolled path, so likely intended.
testing_gaps: No test for controlled changes prevented via defaultPrevented.
No uncontrolled test for dirty/filled/DOM state after details.cancel().
No test for a consumer that rejects or rewrites a controlled value, for controlled null, or for a controlled-to-uncontrolled transition.
No test for onChange validation-mode render count (PR reports 2 renders per keystroke); the render-count test covers only the default validation mode.
No test for a form-reset flow or async/debounced validation with programmatic controlled changes.
